title: Reading the signs of a level
target: How to use the plates a level hangs on its doors in R.E.P.O., given that the arctic station names its own rooms and its own departments.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A level with signs on its doors
Enough light to read a plate
A reason to choose a room

steps.do: Read the plate on a door before committing to the room.
steps.because: the arctic station signs its own rooms, a cafeteria, a research lab and an infirmary among them (arctic sign cafeteria, arctic sign research lab, arctic sign infirmary)

steps.do: Use the working names to find where things are moved.
steps.because: the working side is signed too: a loading dock, a cargo processing area, a staging area and a vehicle maintenance bay (arctic sign loading dock, arctic sign cargo processing, arctic sign staging area)

steps.do: Learn the plant rooms as well.
steps.because: a cooling center and a ventilation chamber each have a plate (arctic sign cooling center, arctic sign ventilation chamber)

steps.do: Read the departments rather than only the rooms.
steps.because: accounting, botanical research and an exotic materials division are named on plates (arctic sign accounting, arctic sign botanical research, arctic sign exotic materials division)

steps.do: Do not skip the living side.
steps.because: living quarters, an observation platform, a recreation room and a testing lab are all signed (arctic sign living quarters, arctic sign observation platform, arctic sign recreation)

steps.do: Expect other themes to ship other sign sheets.
steps.because: a robot company sign, a library sign and a museum no-smoking sign are carried beside the arctic plates (Robot company sign, library sign_DefaultMaterial_BaseColor)

commonMistakes: Opening signed doors at random because the plates look alike.
Treating the plant rooms as part of the working side and skipping them.
Assuming every level uses the same plates as the arctic one.
Walking past a named room because it is small.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
